findings.reason: §11 is the section that owns review task identity, and as written it leaves the plan-review surface keyed by a constant, so its stated outcome does not hold and the section needs to require the reviewed-run element (or the plan identity) for the `plan-review-of-` spelling too.
findings.text: §11 states that a review is "keyed by its own node id rather than by the run it reviews" and has `_task_identity` call the owner predicate so a review keys to the run it reviews; but `_task_identity` derives that run id with `round_node_source(_record_node_id(record), REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX)` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:495-511`), `REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX` is `"review-of-"`, and plan-review nodes are minted `"plan-review-of-<slug>"`. Measured at main 0f72db147 with the repo interpreter: `_task_identity({"node":{"id":"plan-review-of-new-work-gets-a-new-worker","plan":"new-work-gets-a-new-worker"},"role":"review"}, "reckon", [])` returns `('review', 'reckon', '')`, and `plan-review-of-other-plan` returns the identical `('review', 'reckon', '')`, while a `review-of-` id correctly returns `('review', 'reckon', 'shc-potential-rename')`. So every plan-review node in one project collapses onto one key.

findings.reason: it sends §7 down a path where its own selectivity measure silently fails for plan-reviews, which §7's falsifier ("composes a session from a different task") would not catch, so §11 must close it before §7 flips the flag.
findings.text: because that key is constant, `_prior_same_task_run`'s comparison at `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:604` matches any earlier plan-review record in the project, so once §7 restores `session_reuse` a plan-review of one plan composes a prior plan-review's session of a different one — the cross-task reuse this plan exists to remove, on the surface the review reflex actually dispatches under — and §11 neither repairs nor names it.

findings.reason: a done-when that cannot fail on the defect the section is about measures nothing, so the case must pin the resolved element and the control must include a `plan-review-of-` node.
findings.text: the required case pins the record's node id (answering the earlier review) but asserts only that `_task_identity` returns a key whose first element is `"review"`; it does not assert the reviewed-run element, so `('review', <project>, '')` passes and the constant-identity defect above is invisible to the gate, and the named negative control restores the root-only predicate, which exercises the role branch only and cannot fail on the prefix.

findings.reason: the named symbol resolves and a worker greps it, so no work changes.
findings.text: "remove the re-export at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2882`" resolves to line 2881 at main 0f72db147: the §10 commit this section declares it follows (`15dff49be`) deleted the `_capture_member_session` line immediately above it in the same import block, so the anchor is stale by exactly that deletion.
